world.org_type: a shire county council's exchequer service, which runs a first-two-digit filter that routes payments for post-payment examination by a framework assurance provider

driver: The forward count of items a fixed band rule selects includes units outside the band today: each unit's periodic amount is one sum over every component it holds, a filed date in the forward window ends one class of component, and re-summing what survives moves the unit's amount into the selected band; some units are paid in two equal parts to two linked payees, and how a unit is paid depends on how many components it keeps, because the record's own changed units show that a unit left with one component is paid its whole amount by the first payee and nothing by the second; a forecast that treats every linked unit as always paid in halves carries the one-component units' halves below the band's lower floor and out of the count, and only applying the payment rule recovered from the changed units puts each such unit's whole amount into the band once a period, after a fixed-term cohort run-off on a term recovered from an earlier completed cohort, the whole-amount decomposition and the linked-pair re-sum have all been made and read as final.
driver_concrete: Adult Social Care's flagged cell 14 holds the four-weekly 1,464-pound Shared Lives payment for one long-term band 2 guest, and a carer is paid one four-weekly amount for every guest hosted, so after the Home First step-down places close on 31 March 2027 the 60 single carers paid 3,044, 3,272 or 3,524 fall to 1,464 and the 8 jointly approved households paid 2,274, 2,388 or 2,514 a half fall to 1,484 a half; 16 further joint households host a band 2 guest beside a step-down guest (halves 1,522, 1,636 or 1,762) and are left with one guest, and the extract's changed households (November 2023, August 2024, September 2025) show a one-guest household paid its whole fee by the first vendor number and nothing by the second, so each is paid 1,464 once a run in cell 14 rather than two halves of 732 under the 1,000-pound floor: 194 carer payments a run in cell 14 against 102 now, 6,914 routed payments in 2027/28 (filed 6,900) against 6,706 (6,700) with every joint household halved, 6,498 (6,500) with the halves held and 5,718 (5,700) with every carer held (Housing Support's 2024-25 Tenancy Sustainment round run off on its 30-instalment term in all).
stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen until all 63 published figures reproduce, runs Housing Support's 2024-25 instalment intake off on its 30-instalment term, decomposes every Shared Lives carer payment into the scheduled weekly rates (each joint half as two weeks of them), moves the 60 single carers paid 3,044, 3,272 or 3,524 to 1,464 and the 16 halves paid 2,274, 2,388 or 2,514 to 1,484 in cell 14 after the Home First step-down closure on 31 March 2027, carries the 32 halves paid 1,522, 1,636 or 1,762 down to 732 each, under the filter's 1,000-pound floor, and files 6,700 routed payments (6,706); the step that lands it there is reading a joint household as two vendors each paid half of whatever the household is owed, when the extract's own changed households show that a joint household left with one guest is paid its whole fee by the first vendor and nothing by the second, so the 16 households hosting a band 2 guest beside a step-down guest are each paid 1,464 once a run from April 2027, in cell 14, and the plan year routes 6,900 (6,914).

differentiation.task126: Both turn on a population gap and file a quantity, but task125's move is a forward composition inside a forecast (one periodic amount summed over components, a filed closure ends one class, and re-summing what survives puts units into the counted band in the plan year), while task126's is a historical succession link that over-joins units and is split by a separate classification ledger inside a descriptive median; the decisive generator (G2 against G3), Gate G mechanism (forecasting against method_or_model_selection), shape (02 against 14), calibration form, domain and objective all differ.

notes: Realises analytical_tasks note AD02 (analytical_tasks/02_anomaly_detection/AD02_digit-filter-workload-cohort-runoff.md), its first realisation, drawn 2026-10-10; registered after task124 in task-number order. The note's decisive move, Housing Support's fixed-term cohort run off on a term recovered from the completed 2021 intake, is kept as rung 3: the pilot's plain solver replays records at the finest grain and runs cohort studies unprompted, and the 2021 intake's full rise and run-off sits in the same flagged-cell series, so that rung is constructed rather than missed. A first redraw (re-pricing Adult Social Care's stream at a filed 2027/28 tariff) reads honestly as (time, A) or (time, G13) and the guard blocks both (task121 v1 lineage in the window, ten older builds, task122's decisive G13), so the decisive rung moved to the population gap: the forward composition of each carer's single four-weekly payment. Requester moved from the head of internal audit (compliance_or_audit, banned against task119) to the head of exchequer services (finance_controller); internal audit keeps publishing the conformity statements. Context artifact redrawn at registration from close_out_summary (BLOCK ban.artifact against task124) to operations_log, the filter's 2025/26 run log. Harden loop 1 (2026-10-10): round 1's plain solver landed the carer-grain decomposition (rung 4, 6,500), so the decisive rung moved to the household grain (jointly approved households paid in equal halves to consecutive vendor numbers); driver, driver_concrete and stump rewritten to it at stage 3b.
